title: Convergence groups
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: Groups of homeomorphisms of a compact metric space in which every sequence of distinct elements has a subsequence collapsing the space, off one point, to another point. The first lesson proves from the definition by sequences that every element is elliptic, parabolic or loxodromic, describes the dynamics of loxodromic and parabolic elements, and shows that the stabilizer of a fixed point of a loxodromic element is virtually infinite cyclic. The second lesson shows that convergence actions and minimal actions pass to equivariant quotients, and that a convergence group on a compact connected metric space acts as a convergence group on the dendrite quotient of the space. The third lesson attaches to every point of the completion of an invariant set of cut points a closed connected subset of the space, its support, and proves that a minimal action fixes no point of the completion and that a parabolic element whose fixed point is not one of the chosen cut points fixes exactly one point of the completion. The fourth lesson determines the points of the completion fixed by a loxodromic element: at most three points next to each other, or exactly two points without neighbours, far apart, whose supports are the two fixed points of the element. The fifth lesson treats group actions on trees in the language of pretrees, contraction of edges, and the first identification on the completion: for a group with the fixed-point property for trees with finite edge stabilizers, no class of the finite interval relation of the completion is invariant. These are the facts about convergence groups used in OpenAI's proof (2026) of the Singer conjecture in dimension four outside the middle degree.
prerequisites: core course Point-Set Topology (C90): compact metric spaces
from the second lesson on: the course Pretrees (cut points of a connected space, the completion, the dendrite quotient of a continuum)
the course proves every other fact it uses

checks.reading: Each proof was written out and re-read step by step on 11 Oct 2026; statements compared with Section 6 of Bowditch's memoir (author's version, library copy free/authors/bowditch/bhb-treelike.pdf), whose proofs use the action on distinct triples; here every proof uses collapsing sequences. Lesson 2 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against Lemma 6.5 of the memoir and its remarks on naturality (pages 52, 56); the proofs use collapsing sequences; the statement on fixed points in a quotient (Corollary 1.2) and the equivariance of every step of the dendrite quotient are proved in the lesson. Lesson 3 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against Lemmas 6.8, 6.10 and 6.11 of the memoir (pages 58-61); every step was re-derived. The statement that two supports meet in at most one point of T, which the memoir asserts without proof, is proved (Proposition 1.3). Lesson 4 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against Lemma 6.9 of the memoir (pages 59-60); every step was re-derived. Spelled out beyond the memoir: why a connected invariant support with two points contains both fixed points; the exclusion of a third fixed point when an interval is infinite; the connectedness of the auxiliary sets N(p); and the reading of the memoir's 'N(p) = {p}' when p is not a point of T (the one point of N(p) is then a point of T adjacent to p, which contradicts that p has no neighbour). Lesson 5 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against Lemmas 6.7 and 6.12 of the memoir (pages 58, 61); every step was re-derived. The memoir proves Lemma 6.7 by modifying a graph-of-groups argument; the lesson derives it from the fixed-point property by contracting the edges with infinite stabilizers (Propositions 2.1, 2.2). The fixed-point property itself (the memoir's Lemma 6.6 for one-ended groups) is a hypothesis in the lesson.
checks.layout: Measured in the staged pages at column widths 1100, 768, 543 and 375 px on 12 Oct 2026: 1,909 formulas in the five lessons, none wider than the column, no TeX errors.

open_obligations: Not yet in the course: the theorem that the dendrite quotient is not a point when a cut point is not a parabolic fixed point (Bowditch, Lemma 6.13 and Theorem 6.1).

Hypothesis without a provider in the programme: the fixed-point property for trees with finite edge stabilizers holds for finitely generated groups with one end (Bowditch, Lemma 6.6; needs groups acting on trees and ends of groups).
Not in the course: the equivalence of the definition by sequences with proper discontinuity on distinct triples.
free_sources: B. H. Bowditch, Treelike structures arising from continua and convergence groups (author's version of Mem. Amer. Math. Soc. 662, 1999), Section 6
